extracted.intended_audience: artists (writers, visual artists, composers, choreographers) and prospective residency applicants; general public researching artist residencies
extracted.subtask_description: Information and implicit criteria about the Ucross Foundation artist residency program — who it serves, what facilities and time it provides, and the program's values and opportunities. Useful for prospective applicants to understand eligibility, length, facilities, and institutional priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ucross Foundation operates a retreat for visual artists, writers, composers, and choreographers working in all creative disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program explicitly supports multiple creative disciplines (visual art, writing, composition, choreography); applicants should be creators within these fields. The phrase 'working in all creative disciplines' suggests openness to cross-disciplinary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation provides ... to competitively selected individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is competitive — applicants should expect peer or jury-based selection rather than open enrollment. No explicit selection criteria are listed on the page, but competitive selection implies review of artistic merit, fit, and proposal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency duration and cohort size
rubrics_metrics.description: Residencies run for two to six weeks. Up to ten individuals are in residence at any one time. Approximately 115 individuals are supported annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan projects that can progress in a concentrated 2–6 week period and consider the small simultaneous cohort (up to 10) when proposing collaborations or community engagement. Annual throughput gives a sense of competitiveness and program scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studio and facility availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation has four writing studios, four visual arts studios, and two composing studios and the Lauren Anderson Dance Studio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in need of dedicated studio space should note the specific counts and types of studios. The presence of specialized spaces (dance studio, composing studios) indicates institutional support for particular modes of work; applicants should state any studio needs in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living accommodations and on-site housing
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists in residence live in their studios, the historic Ucross School House or the Clearmont Train Depot, which have been renovated to include four bedrooms each, with a dining area, living area, and main kitchen in the School House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency includes on-site housing with shared living spaces; applicants should be prepared for communal living and to work from on-site accommodations. Project planning should account for this living arrangement and limited private housing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uninterrupted time and setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation provides ... uninterrupted time in the High Plains landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The retreat emphasizes solitude and time away from regular obligations; applicants should propose work that benefits from concentrated, distraction-free periods and may reference the High Plains environment as part of their project (research, inspiration, site-specific work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition and public programming opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The renovated Ucross Art Gallery ... operates year-round at no cost to the public and typically features exhibitions by Ucross Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows may have opportunities for exhibitions and public-facing programming. Applicants whose work benefits from public exhibition or engagement should highlight readiness to exhibit or present work produced during residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations and professional partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation participates in a number of long-term collaborations with other arts organizations, including the Sundance Institute Theatre Program, the Herb Alpert Award in the Arts ..., the PEN/Hemingway Award for Debut Novel, and others (Alley Theatre, Pew Fellowships, Whiting Foundation, UCLA’s Center for the Art of Performance, Yale University, Shepherd School of Music at Rice, Cave Canem, Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program maintains extensive partnerships that may create additional fellowship pathways, prizes, or professional opportunities; applicants should note any affiliation-based eligibility or benefits and consider referencing partnerships that align with their practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional values: land stewardship and conservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ucross has supported numerous conservation initiatives, including the planting of thousands of trees on the ranch and the placement of a conservation easement on over 12,000 acres of the ranch ... The Park at Ucross hosts a small interdenominational chapel and The Raymond Plank Center, a modern structure that hosts art exhibitions, artists in residence, and regional and national conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation emphasizes land stewardship and conservation as part of its mission; applicants whose work engages with landscape, ecology, or community stewardship may find alignment and should consider addressing how their project interacts with these values.
